words.sense: selfless concern expressed in personally costly help without expected reward
misconceptions: Assuming altruism and philanthropy mean the same thing whenever both appear relevant.
Ignoring the defining evidence needed for philanthropy.

words.sense: organized donation of resources for the good of others or the public
misconceptions: Assuming altruism and philanthropy mean the same thing whenever both appear relevant.
Ignoring the defining evidence needed for altruism.

semantic_axes.description: Altruism highlights selfless help despite personal cost; philanthropy highlights structured giving of resources for wider benefit.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Nadia’s decision at the station?

beats.text: Nadia gave her last bus fare to a stranded classmate and walked the long route home without asking for anything back.
beats.decisive_clue: personal sacrifice made without expected return
beats.reason: Personal sacrifice made without expected return is the strongest evidence for altruism here.

beats.text: She never told anyone else why she had walked home that evening.
beats.decisive_clue: personal sacrifice made without expected return; private nature of the story does not change that
beats.reason: She spent something she needed to help another person; the absence of publicity changes nothing.

chains.feedback_short: Personal sacrifice made without expected return still decides; the later detail does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: Altruism means selfless concern expressed in personally costly help without expected reward; philanthropy means organized donation of resources for the good of others or the public. She spent something she needed to help another person; the absence of publicity changes nothing.
chains.contrast_rule: Altruism: helps without seeking repayment; philanthropy: pooled giving distributed systematically.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Lian’s scholarship initiative?

beats.text: Lian created a fund where many donors contribute money and a committee awards grants to students each term.
beats.decisive_clue: pooled donations administered through a grant committee
beats.reason: Pooled donations administered through a grant committee is the strongest evidence for philanthropy here.

beats.text: The group now publishes yearly figures for collected donations and awarded grants.
beats.decisive_clue: pooled donations administered through a grant committee; further evidence: regular public accounting of contributions and awards
beats.reason: The repeated, structured distribution of pooled resources makes this organized giving.

chains.feedback_short: Regular public accounting of contributions and awards confirms the earlier clue: pooled donations administered through a grant committee.
chains.feedback_deep: Altruism means selfless concern expressed in personally costly help without expected reward; philanthropy means organized donation of resources for the good of others or the public. The repeated, structured distribution of pooled resources makes this organized giving.
chains.contrast_rule: Altruism: helps without seeking repayment; philanthropy: pooled giving distributed systematically.

hints.attention: Look at the funding structure and decisions.
hints.axis: Altruism highlights selfless help despite personal cost; philanthropy highlights structured giving of resources for wider benefit.
hints.contrast: Altruism: helps without seeking repayment; philanthropy: pooled giving distributed systematically.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Rafi’s choice to tutor a younger student?

beats.text: Rafi gave up his free Saturdays to tutor a younger student and refused the offered fee.
beats.decisive_clue: costly unpaid help with no expected reward
beats.reason: Costly unpaid help with no expected reward is the strongest evidence for altruism here.

beats.text: Rafi enjoyed hearing a grateful thank-you after each session, but still turned down every offer of payment.
beats.decisive_clue: costly unpaid help with no expected reward; gratitude received without any agreed reward does not change that
beats.reason: Enjoying thanks does not erase his costly decision to help without expecting compensation.

chains.feedback_short: Costly unpaid help with no expected reward still decides; the later detail does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: Altruism means selfless concern expressed in personally costly help without expected reward; philanthropy means organized donation of resources for the good of others or the public. Enjoying thanks does not erase his costly decision to help without expecting compensation.
chains.contrast_rule: Altruism: helps without seeking repayment; philanthropy: pooled giving distributed systematically.

hints.attention: Was he acting for something in return?

chains.frame: Which word best describes Sofia’s neighbourhood book initiative?

beats.text: Sofia set up a monthly fund into which residents pay, and its elected volunteers buy books for free public shelves.
beats.decisive_clue: formal pooling of money for public book access
beats.reason: Formal pooling of money for public book access is the strongest evidence for philanthropy here.

beats.text: Sofia gave the initiative a cheerful blue logo, while the monthly collection and book deliveries continued.
beats.decisive_clue: formal pooling of money for public book access; initiative gained a cheerful logo does not change that
beats.reason: A new logo does not change the organized donation and public distribution of books.

chains.feedback_short: Formal pooling of money for public book access still decides; the later detail does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: Altruism means selfless concern expressed in personally costly help without expected reward; philanthropy means organized donation of resources for the good of others or the public. A new logo does not change the organized donation and public distribution of books.
chains.contrast_rule: Altruism: helps without seeking repayment; philanthropy: pooled giving distributed systematically.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Esma’s choice after helping an older neighbour?

beats.text: Already late for an appointment, Esma carried the neighbour’s groceries upstairs and waved away payment.
beats.decisive_clue: sacrificed scarce time while refusing compensation
beats.reason: Sacrificed scarce time while refusing compensation is the strongest evidence for altruism here.

beats.text: When offered a signed volunteer-hours slip afterward, she politely declined that too.
beats.decisive_clue: also declined proof that could benefit her
beats.reason: The later refusal confirms the original action was done for the neighbour rather than personal credit.

chains.feedback_short: Also declined proof that could benefit her makes altruism the better choice.
chains.feedback_deep: Altruism means selfless concern expressed in personally costly help without expected reward; philanthropy means organized donation of resources for the good of others or the public. The later refusal confirms the original action was done for the neighbour rather than personal credit.
chains.contrast_rule: Altruism: helps without seeking repayment; philanthropy: pooled giving distributed systematically.

hints.attention: Look at what she gives up, then at what she refuses.
hints.axis: Altruism highlights selfless help despite personal cost; philanthropy highlights structured giving of resources for wider benefit.
hints.contrast: Altruism: helps without seeking repayment; philanthropy: pooled giving distributed systematically.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Hugo’s coat-giving project?

beats.text: Hugo arranged regular staff donations, logged each contribution and distributed purchased coats through community centres.
beats.decisive_clue: organized collection and allocation of donated resources
beats.reason: Organized collection and allocation of donated resources is the strongest evidence for philanthropy here.

beats.text: The project now partners with local charities to choose where its next batch of coats will go.
beats.decisive_clue: organized collection and allocation of donated resources; further evidence: established distribution partners for later rounds
beats.reason: The continuing coordinated resource-giving, not any one giver’s motive, is what stands out.

chains.feedback_short: Established distribution partners for later rounds confirms the earlier clue: organized collection and allocation of donated resources.
